title: Straight-line forms & angle between lines
examples: What is the easiest form to use when finding the distance from a point to a line?
Can you show me how to find the angle between two lines that are not perpendicular?
If a line passes through the origin, what is its equation in intercept form?

explain.say: Today we learn about equations for straight lines. We will look at several useful forms.

draw.text: Straight Line Forms: Point-Slope, Intercept, Normal

explain.say: The point-slope form uses a known point and the gradient. It is y minus y equals m times x minus x.
For example, a line through point two, three with gradient four. The equation is y minus three equals four times x minus two.
The intercept form uses the x and y intercepts. It is one over x plus one over y equals one over the gradient.
For instance, a line crossing at three on x and five on y. The equation is one over three plus one over five equals one over the gradient.

faq.q: When should I use the point-slope form instead of the slope-intercept form?
faq.a: Use point-slope form when you are given a point and the gradient, but not the y-intercept. It is very direct.
asks: What if I know a point and the slope?
Which form is best if I have coordinates?

faq.q: What is the difference between the intercept form and the slope-intercept form?
faq.a: The intercept form uses the x-intercept and y-intercept directly. The slope-intercept form uses the y-intercept and the gradient.
asks: How do I find the equation if I only have the intercepts?

faq.q: How do I find the distance from a point to a line using these forms?
faq.a: You must first convert the line equation into the general form, ax plus by plus c equals zero. Then use the distance formula.
asks: What is the general form of a line equation?
Is there a formula just for distance?

faq.q: What does the normal form represent for a line?
faq.a: The normal form uses the perpendicular distance from the origin and the gradient. It is a specialized form for certain calculations.
asks: What is the normal form equation?
Does normal form always involve the origin?

faq.q: If the line is horizontal or vertical, which form works best?
faq.a: A horizontal line has a gradient of zero, making the point-slope form simple. A vertical line has an undefined gradient, making the general form best.
asks: What is the equation for a vertical line?
Can the point-slope form handle vertical lines?

facts: The general form of a straight line equation is ax plus by plus c equals zero.
The gradient, or slope, is represented by the letter m.
The y-intercept is the point where the line crosses the y-axis.
The x-intercept is the point where the line crosses the x-axis.

quiz.say: A line passes through point one, two and has a gradient of three. What is its equation in point-slope form?
quiz.why: The point-slope form requires you to substitute the given point coordinates and the gradient directly into the formula.

wrong.1: This incorrectly calculates the y-intercept by substituting x equals one into the equation.
wrong.2: This incorrectly swaps the coordinates when setting up the point-slope form.
wrong.3: This assumes the line passes through the origin, which is not stated.

quiz.say: A line has x-intercept four and y-intercept two. What is its equation using the intercept form?
quiz.why: The intercept form requires you to use the reciprocal of the x-intercept and the y-intercept in the formula.

wrong.0: This incorrectly uses the slope-intercept form without first finding the gradient.
wrong.1: This incorrectly adds the intercepts together instead of keeping them separate in the formula.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes the line passes through the origin.

quiz.say: Find the distance from the point three, four to the line passing through one, one and two, three.
quiz.why: First, find the line equation, then convert it to ax plus by plus c equals zero, and finally apply the distance formula.

wrong.0: This incorrectly uses the gradient of the line to estimate the distance.
wrong.2: This incorrectly calculates the distance using the simple distance formula between the two points.
wrong.3: This calculates the distance between the point and the origin, ignoring the line.
